tasks.title: A tank shell's death jigs: any vehicle killer reads as machine gun
tasks.why: P2, AnimationController.Gags.cs:26. `MachineGun = killer && !crushed && (vehicle || w.Archetype[b] == Machinegunner)` is true for EVERY armed vehicle killer, not for a machine's small arms as the comment on :25 claims. DeathGags.cs:208 tests g.MachineGun BEFORE g.Heavy (:214), so a man killed by a tank's main gun or a flamer vehicle gets DeathGag.Jig (a delayed shudder, thrown 2-5 m) instead of the DeathGag.Punt a heavy hit is meant to give (5-9 m, 1-2 flips). Since vehicles are most of what kills hard, the Punt gag is largely unreachable against a machine, and the heavy hit the player just watched lands as a twitch. Costs: the absurd-deaths work the owner asked for on 2026-10-19 reads wrong at exactly its loudest moment.
tasks.done_when: An EditMode test on DeathGags.Choose (pure, no scene) that is RED on today's code: a GagInput from a vehicle killer with Heavy true must choose DeathGag.Punt, not DeathGag.Jig; and a real Machinegunner kill must still choose Jig.

tasks.title: The prop editor's Scene view draws small props the game hides
tasks.why: P2, BattlefieldProps.cs:447 and :449. The game camera's cull gates a small module (finite module.MaxDistance) on `SceneHooks.CloseUp > 0f && ... <= reach*reach` (:447), but editorSeen (:449) keeps only the distance half and drops the CloseUp gate entirely. CloseUp is 0 from zoom 28 out (TacticalCamera.CloseUpAt), so in the Scene view while props are edited (EditorCamera, :16) every small prop draws at every zoom, while the player's camera never draws it at the same spot. Costs: the owner and the env agents place, space and judge the near dressing against a view that shows props the match does not.
tasks.done_when: The two cull expressions are factored into one static predicate (module reach, page bounds, eye, closeUp) and an EditMode test asserts it answers the same for the game eye and the editor eye at closeUp 0 and 1; red today, because :449 has no closeUp term to pass.

tasks.title: The gore probe counts pieces thrown before the pool exists
tasks.why: P2, DebrisRenderer.cs:272. `Watch?.Invoke(piece, scale, tint)` sits one line ABOVE `if (!Ready) return;` (:273), so the probe reports every piece as thrown even when Start never ran (no TW/Debris shader, :230, or the component disabled) and nothing is pooled or drawn. GoreZoomStills.cs:109-146 is built entirely on that probe and its only assertion is `sizes.Count >= WantSamples` (:144) with the message 'nobody is bleeding'. So the one test that measures the drawn gore against the drawn man can go green, and write a gore.txt of sizes, on a run where not one piece reached the GPU. Costs: the owner's 'the gore is sometimes a bit big' (tasks.md:597) is being answered from numbers the render never saw.
tasks.done_when: The Invoke moves below the Ready gate, and an EditMode test on a DebrisRenderer whose Start never ran (Ready false) sets Watch, calls Throw, and asserts the probe fired 0 times; red today, where it fires once.

tasks.title: A crouched man firing above 1.6 m/s slides his feet
tasks.why: P2, AnimationController.cs:792 (new on bdfed04ff3). `gait = firing && speed < 2.2f ? Clip.FireStoop : speed > 1.8f ? Clip.CrouchRun : ...` puts a firing man on FireStoop all the way to 2.2 m/s, but FireStoop is authored at 1 m/s (Clips.Table, :76) and the rate clamp at :811 stops at 1.6, so from 1.6 to 2.2 m/s his feet run up to 37 % slower than the ground moving under him. The comment on :790 says 'above that the crouched run wins, nobody fires at that pace' -- but the FireStoop branch is tested FIRST, so CrouchRun (authored 2.4 m/s, the clip that would fit) is unreachable for any firing man below 2.2. Costs: visible skating on every crouched advance-and-fire, the pose this commit was written to add.
tasks.done_when: An EditMode test over the gait choice asserts a firing crouched man at 2.1 m/s is given CrouchRun (or FireStoop at a rate the clamp actually reaches), and at 1.2 m/s still FireStoop; red today, where 2.1 m/s gives FireStoop at rate 1.6.
